verdict.rationale: PagerDuty documents an official MCP server that lets AI assistants securely manage incidents. Its Events API v2 explicitly supports follow-up events to acknowledge or resolve alerts, and its REST API lets third parties manipulate account data, so acknowledging and resolving without the dashboard is documented. Escalation is only shown as automatic behaviour driven by escalation policies, not as an action an agent can invoke through the API or MCP. missing for 10: an explicit API/MCP escalate or reassign action, a documented MCP tool list covering acknowledge/escalate/resolve, independent hands-on corroboration of an agent running the full lifecycle.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can acknowledge, escalate, and resolve incidents end to end through a documented API or MCP connection — no dashboard in the loop

citations.quote: Connect AI tools to PagerDuty with MCP to securely manage incidents
enables AI assistants (like Claude Desktop, Cursor, or VS Code) to interact securely with your PagerDuty account
Follow up events can be sent to acknowledge or resolve an existing alert.
The REST API provides a way for third parties to connect to a PagerDuty account and access or manipulate configuration data on that account.
Trigger, acknowledge, and resolve incidents created by service integrations.
